name: TX-30
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strongly Democratic district (PVI D+25) after redistricting
Haynes outraised Jackson roughly 24-to-1 with outside support
Open seat with no polling, but fundamentals dominate
model.rationale: The post-redistricting D+25 baseline and prediction markets both point to a safe Democratic hold, and the massive fundraising gap reinforces it. With no contrary evidence, I keep the baseline margin and tighten uncertainty slightly.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing a single-digit race or unexpected Republican outside spending would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Texas's 30th District is an open seat after redistricting drew it as a strongly Democratic, majority-Black district with a D+25 partisan lean. Frederick Haynes III enters as the clear favorite, having raised over $420,000 with about $200,000 in outside support, while Republican Everett Jackson has raised under $18,000 with minimal cash on hand.

There is no public general-election polling and no expert ratings, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals, the fundraising imbalance, and prediction markets, which price the Democratic nominee around 96%. The baseline model's D+26 margin is retained, with uncertainty narrowed modestly given the consistent signals. The seat is rated Safe Democratic.
